# 2 Kings Chapter 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 243r–243v

---

**22:1** A-son of-eight years [was] Yoshiyyahu when-he-became-king, and-thirty and-one years he-reigned in-Yerushalayim. And-the-name of-his-mother [was] Yedidah daughter of-Adayah from-Botsqat.

**22:2** And-he-did the-right [ha-yashar] in-the-eyes of-YHWH, and-he-walked in-all the-way of-David his-father, and-he-did-not turn [lo sar] right or-left.

**22:3** And-it-was in-the-eighteenth year [bi-shemoneh esreh shanah] of-the-king Yoshiyyahu, the-king sent Shaphan son of-Atsalyahu son of-Meshullam, the-scribe [ha-sofer], to-the-house of-YHWH, saying:

**22:4** Go-up to Chilqiyyahu the-great priest [ha-kohen ha-gadol], and-let-him-reckon [veyattem] the-silver [ha-kesef] which-has-been-brought [ha-muva] to-the-house of-YHWH, which the-keepers of-the-threshold [shomrey ha-saf] have-gathered from the-people.

**22:5** And-let-them-give-it into-the-hand of-the-doers of-the-work [osey ha-melakhah] who-are-appointed [ha-mufqadim] in-the-house of-YHWH, and-let-them-give it to-the-doers of-the-work who [are] in-the-house of-YHWH, to-repair [le-chazeq] the-breach [bedeq] of-the-house:

**22:6** To-the-craftsmen [la-charashim] and-to-the-builders [la-bonim] and-to-the-masons [la-goderim], and-to-buy timber ['etsim] and-hewn stones [avney machtsev] to-repair the-house.

**22:7** Only [akh], the-silver given into-their-hand was-not reckoned-with-them [lo yechashev ittam], for in-faithfulness [be-emunah] they [were] working.

**22:8** And-said Chilqiyyahu the-great priest to Shaphan the-scribe: The-book of-the-Torah [sefer ha-torah] I-have-found in-the-house of-YHWH. And-gave Chilqiyyahu the-book to-Shaphan, and-he-read-it [vayiqra'ehu].

**22:9** And-came Shaphan the-scribe to the-king and-returned the-king a-word [davar] and-said: Your-servants have-poured-out [hitikhu] the-silver which-was-found in-the-house, and-have-given-it into-the-hand of-the-doers of-the-work who-are-appointed in-the-house of-YHWH.

**22:10** And-told Shaphan the-scribe to-the-king, saying: A-book [sefer] Chilqiyyahu the-priest has-given to-me. And-read-it [vayiqra'ehu] Shaphan before the-king.

**22:11** And-it-was when-the-king heard the-words of-the-book of-the-Torah, and-he-tore [vayiqra'] his-garments [begadayv].

**22:12** And-commanded the-king Chilqiyyahu the-priest and-Achiqam son of-Shaphan and-'Akhbor son of-Mikhayah and-Shaphan the-scribe and-'Asayah servant of-the-king, saying:

**22:13** Go, inquire [dirshu] of-YHWH on-my-behalf [ba'adi] and-on-behalf-of the-people and-on-behalf-of all Yehudah, concerning the-words of-this book which-has-been-found. For great [gedolah] is the-wrath [ha-chemah] of-YHWH which is-kindled [nitstsah] against-us, because our-fathers did-not listen to the-words of-this book, to-do according-to-all which-is-written concerning-us.

**22:14** And-went Chilqiyyahu the-priest and-Achiqam and-'Akhbor and-Shaphan and-'Asayah to Chuldah the-prophetess [ha-nevi'ah], wife of-Shallum son of-Tiqvah son of-Charchas, keeper of-the-garments [shomer ha-begadim]. And-she [was] dwelling in-Yerushalayim in-the-Second-Quarter [ba-Mishneh]. And-they-spoke to-her.

**22:15** And-she-said to-them: Thus says YHWH, God of-Yisra'el: Say to-the-man who-sent you to-me:

**22:16** Thus says YHWH: Behold, I [am] bringing evil [ra'ah] upon this place and-upon its-inhabitants, all the-words of-the-book which the-king of-Yehudah has-read.

**22:17** Because [tachat asher] they-have-abandoned-me [azavuni] and-burned-incense [vayeqatteru] to-other gods, in-order-to-provoke-me-to-anger [le-ma'an hakh'iseni] with-all the-work of-their-hands, and-my-wrath [chamati] shall-be-kindled against this place and-shall-not be-quenched [lo tikhbeh].

**22:18** And-to the-king of-Yehudah, the-one-sending you to-inquire of-YHWH, thus shall-you-say to-him: Thus says YHWH, God of-Yisra'el: The-words which you-have-heard —

**22:19** Because [ya'an] your-heart was-tender [rakh] and-you-humbled-yourself [vatikkana'] before YHWH when-you-heard what I-spoke against this place and-against its-inhabitants — to-become a-desolation [le-shammah] and-a-curse [ve-li-qelalah] — and-you-tore your-garments and-you-wept before-me, and-I-also [gam anokhi] have-heard, declares [ne'um] YHWH.

**22:20** Therefore, behold, I-will-gather-you [osifkha] to your-fathers, and-you-shall-be-gathered to-your-tomb in-peace [be-shalom], and-your-eyes shall-not see all the-evil which I [am] bringing upon this place. And-they-returned the-king the-word.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.8 — sefer ha-torah:** "The Book of the Torah" — almost certainly a form of Deuteronomy, or at least its core legal section (Deut 12-26). The discovery narrative is the central event of Josiah's reign and the Deuteronomistic history's pivotal moment.

**v.14 — Chuldah the prophetess:** Despite the availability of Jeremiah and Zephaniah (both active during Josiah's reign), the delegation consults Huldah. Her authority as *nevi'ah* is unquestioned. She lives in the *Mishneh* (Second Quarter), the newer extension of Jerusalem's western hill.

**v.19 — "your heart was tender":** The adjective *rakh* (tender, soft) contrasts with the hardness (*qasheh*) attributed to the hearts of disobedient kings. Josiah's response to the Torah — tearing garments, weeping — is the proper human response to divine revelation.

**v.20 — "gathered to your fathers in peace":** An ironic promise, since Josiah will die violently at Megiddo (23:29). The narrator does not resolve this tension. "Peace" may refer to the fact that Jerusalem's destruction does not occur during his lifetime.

*— EMET*
